Rashi on Nedarim 7a:1:1.english: Of you - [As the verse states:] “For the Lord your God will surely require it of you” (Deuteronomy 23:22).

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:2:1.hebrew: לנפקותא בעלמא - כלומר, והדין זוז אחר ליהוי לי להוצאה; ודבורא הוא דלא אסקיה, דלא גמר דיבורו דאמר: עלי לנפקותא:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:2:1.english: Merely for general use - That is to say: “And this other coin shall be for my expenses”; and it was merely speech that he did not complete, as he did not finish his statement to say: “It is for my expenses.”

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:3:1.hebrew: דכתיב בפיך - "כאשר דברת בפיך", וכתיב: "יצא מפי צדקה" (ישעיהו מ״ה:כ״ג):
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:3:1.english: As it is written: “With your mouth” - [As in the verse:] “[...Which] you spoke with your mouth” (Deuteronomy 23:24), [and it is written:] “Righteousness has gone forth from My mouth” (Isaiah 45:23).

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:5:1.hebrew: או דלמא שאני צדקה - להכי אית לה יד, דלא חזיא אלא לעניים. אבל הפקר, דהא נמי אפי' לעשירים חזי — מי אמרת דיש להן יד:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:5:1.english: Or perhaps charity is different - For this reason it has an intimation, as it is suitable only for the poor. But ownerless property, which is indeed suitable even for the wealthy — do you say that they have an intimation?

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:1.hebrew: הפקר היינו צדקה - דסתם מפקיר בשביל שיזכו בה עניים, ומסיק: מ"מ הפקר הוי לעניים ולעשירים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:1.english: Ownerless property is charity - For ordinarily one declares property ownerless so that the poor will acquire it, and the Gemara concludes: Nevertheless, ownerless property is for both the poor and the rich.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:2.hebrew: ואם תמצא לומר דאין היקש למחצה - וא"ת: שפיר קאמר דאין היקש למחצה, ומאי מיבעיא ליה גבי צדקה? י"ל: דשאני הכא, דסברא הוא שלא לעשות ההיקש אלא לענין "בל תאחר" הכתוב שם; שהרי כמה דברים הכתובים באותו פסוק שחלוקים זה מזה בכמה ענינים, ולא נכתב שם אלא לענין "בל תאחר":
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:2.english: "And if you say that there is no partial analogy based on juxtaposition" - And if you say: The Gemara rightly says that there is no partial analogy, and why did it raise a dilemma with regard to charity? One can say: It is different here, for it stands to reason not to apply the analogy except with regard to the matter of "you shall not delay" that is written there; for behold, several things are written in that verse that differ from one another in several matters, and it was written there only with regard to the matter of "you shall not delay".

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:3.hebrew: הפקר היינו צדקה - דסתם מפקיר בשביל שיזכו בה עניים, ומסיק: מ"מ הפקר הוי לעניים ולעשירים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:3.english: Ownerless property is charity - For typically one who declares property ownerless does so in order that the poor may acquire it; and the Gemara concludes: nevertheless, ownerless property is for both the poor and the wealthy.
